notes.meaning: David cries out urgently to the Lord in deep distress, knowing that human help is useless. He begs God to hurry to his aid and listen closely to his plea. Believers can call on God with this same boldness whenever trouble presses in.

David asks God to accept his personal prayer just like the fragrant incense burned daily in the sanctuary. Being far away from the altar, he offers his lifted hands as his evening sacrifice of devotion. Lifting empty hands was a common way to pray, showing humble dependence on God to supply every need.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: In Orthodox evening worship (Vespers), this verse is chanted while incense is offered, showing that believers' prayers rise acceptably to God through Christ.

notes.meaning: Under heavy pressure from his enemies, David asks God to station a guard over his mouth. He knows how easy it is to speak foolishly, complain against God, or lash out in anger when provoked. Asking God to shut the door of our lips helps keep our words pure.

David prays that God will protect his inner thoughts so his heart is not drawn toward wickedness. He refuses to share in the delicacies of evil men, which means turning down the perks, pleasures, and profits gained through sin. He asks for strength to resist tempting compromises before they take root.

David welcomes the honest correction of a godly person, calling it an act of loving kindness. He compares such a rebuke to soothing oil poured on the head, which heals rather than harms. Even while accepting loving correction, he continues to pray against the evil deeds of the wicked.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Ancient translations like the Septuagint and Latin Vulgate read the middle line as a warning against being seduced by the smooth flatteries of the wicked, translating it as 'let not the oil of the sinner anoint my head.'

notes.meaning: When wicked leaders are finally judged and brought down, the people they misled will open their ears to David's words. Suffering and defeat often strip away pride and prepare the heart to welcome wise guidance. Truth that was once rejected can become sweet when people see the ruin of corrupt leaders.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars find the Hebrew phrasing here and in verse 7 so difficult and abrupt that they consider the lines to be displaced from another context.

notes.meaning: David describes his companions as being pushed to the brink of death, scattered like plowed dirt or wood chips outside a grave. Their situation looked completely broken and helpless in the eyes of the world. Yet just as plowed soil is torn open so new crops can grow, this deep trial still holds hope for new life.

Even with death staring him in the face, David keeps his eyes firmly set on the Sovereign Lord. He runs to God for shelter and begs Him not to spill out his life or leave him defenseless. Looking directly to God keeps faith strong in the middle of severe danger.

David asks the Lord to guard his steps so he does not fall into the hidden traps set by evil people. Enemies were actively plotting his downfall through secret schemes and tempting lures. Only God's watchful eye can keep a believer safe from hazards they cannot see.

David asks that the wicked get caught in the very nets they spread for others, while he slips past unharmed. Instead of taking personal revenge, he leaves justice in God's hands. God consistently protects the innocent and causes evil plans to backfire on those who make them.
